claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
Incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces cause stress concentration, interfacial cracking, and brittleness in the initial alloy.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform coarse FCC/B2 lamellae into a hierarchical patterned microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will produce coherent FCC/B2 interfaces and refined lamellar spacing.
High pressure and temperature enhance atomic diffusion and stress-induced interface migration.
Pressure-enhanced diffusion and interface migration reduce interfacial energy and eliminate incoherent boundaries.
Coherent interfaces lower the barrier for dislocation transmission between FCC and B2.
Dislocations will transfer between the soft FCC phase and the hard B2 phase without causing premature crack initiation.
The coherent hierarchical structure will activate dislocation slip, stacking faults, and twinning.
The activated deformation mechanisms will homogenize strain distribution and enhance strain hardening and ductility.
The hierarchical coherent structure will arrest interfacial cracking and overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The HPHT-treated alloy will attain elongation greater than 20% while retaining an ultimate tensile strength greater than 1.0 GPa.
The treated fracture surfaces will exhibit elongated cracks and dimples rather than isolated microcracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain.
The untreated baseline has less than 10% elongation while retaining high strength.
Excessive pressure or temperature could dissolve the B2 phase, form amorphous phases, or cause excessive grain growth that degrades strength.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during the HPHT treatment.
